subject: Validity of LOO when summing log-likelihood over trials

messages.author: cddc0fd901f3e12a
messages.subject: Validity of LOO when summing log-likelihood over trials
parts:
Hi everyone! I'm new to the Stan world and I have a question on model comparison via LOO. 

I noticed that in almost every hBayesDM Stan model, the log-likelihood is calculated by participant, summing the trial-by-trial log-likelihoods for each subject. This makes sense to me, as single trials are not independent of each other. 

However, for hierarchical models, shouldn't the LOO procedure involve re-fitting the model without the left-out participant, on every iteration? If so, how can this be achieved? If not, why so?

Thanks!

messages.author: c437e8fd9359a95f
messages.subject: Re: Validity of LOO when summing log-likelihood over trials
parts:
Hi,
LOO return by Stan is not the real "leave one participant out cross validation", Loo approximate the real cross validation by using importance sampling algorithm. For details, you can check this paper:

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., and Gabry, J. (2017a). Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. Statistics and Computing. 27(5), 1413--1432. doi:10.1007/s11222-016-9696-4 (journal version, preprint arXiv:1507.04544).
